use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: C2 JU
When the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

The dual designation has been resolved via correlation: the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point, and the receiving IUs have retained the designated Retained TN and dropped the designated Dropped TN.

Upon correlation execution, the Retained TN has been updated with the Dropped TN's Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength (if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track).

Identification data has been transferred to the Retained TN in accordance with ID conflict restrictions: if the transfer is restricted and the IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN has been processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, the specific ID/IAD and platform attributes have been transferred.
Any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN has been transferred to the Retained TN where the corresponding data for the Retained TN is zero.
If the originating C2 JU held R2 for the Dropped TN, it has dropped the Dropped TN and transmitted a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message after the J7.2 message.
If the correlation was a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
If the own unit held the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN has been designated as a common local track upon successful correlation execution.

If automatic correlation is allowed under the J10.2 Engagement Status exception (either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track's ID is Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track's ID is Friend), the Unknown/Hostile track has been designated as the Dropped TN (TN-2).

Two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, having passed the required correlation tests and restrictions (including the course, speed, and altitude differential tests) before correlation is executed.
The C2 JU holds the locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, boost indication) and the corresponding interface-reported data for the two tracks needed to perform the correlation comparison.

The C2 JU wants to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation, so that each reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The C2 JU wants to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation, so that each reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation; the C2 JU correlates them, resolving the dual designation so the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The C2 JU has two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The two tracks have been correlated and the dual designation is resolved; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
in_scope_actions: Correlating two eligible tracks reported to the interface
Resolving the dual designation via track correlation
excluded_adjacent_actions: PPLI-based reduction of surveillance track redundancy
General protocol-level minimization of dual-designation occurrences and duration
Post-correlation data transfer, drop-track messaging, or downstream interface reporting

claims.content: At the point where correlation is attempted, if a dual designation arises from an initial report on ballistic missile contacts, track merging, simultaneous multiple launches, registration errors, time-of-observation differences, or high velocity contacts, these situations are most likely to lead to dual ballistic missile designations and may cause the correlation to fail or produce erroneous results; accordingly, if it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation should occur as the exception-handling outcome.
At the correlation test, if the correlation test would occur more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time, the correlation test is outside the required timing window.

If the C2 JU attempts a manual correlation of two tracks and the tracks are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote, the manual correlation shall not be performed.

At the correlation acceptance step, if a prespecified condition exists that requires or allows the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation, the requested correlation is rejected; whenever a correlation request is rejected, a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 is transmitted to report the rejection.

Upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message, if the receiving JU holds OCCs on both subject tracks or holds conflicting IDs on the two tracks when the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled, the receiving JU shall reject the correlation.

At the correlation acceptance step, if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, automatic correlation may be allowed despite the normal restriction.

If a ballistic missile track is lost (the JU with R2 has received no local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or determines the track is lost by other system criteria) and the lost track is reported with Lost Track Indicator set to 1, the reporting JU is assumed to have a TQ of 5 less than that being reported; the exception-handling outcome is that a JU holding Tracking data may assume R2 with a TQ of 11 (for example, a reported Lost Track at TQ 15 corresponds to Tracking data at TQ 11).
If it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation should occur.

The C2 JU uses its automatic correlation capability to continuously correlate locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG; when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action to resolve the dual designation.

When correlation is initiated manually, the C2 JU may correlate any two tracks irrespective of the automatic correlation test criteria and restrictions; in this case, it transmits the J7.2 Correlation message with the RV field set to 3, requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks and identifying the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, and the receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless a prespecified rejection condition applies.
Upon receipt of each remote real-time track not confirmed to have an existing correlation, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track, the C2 JU makes an automatic correlation test.
In the automatic correlation test, the C2 JU compares locally derived sensor data (e.g., position, velocity, altitude, and boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, the C2 JU deems them a tentative correlation.
The same two tracks are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.

When the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and no correlation restriction applies, they have passed the correlation tests and restrictions twice and are processed for dual designation resolution.

The recognizing C2 JU initiates transmission of the J7.2 Correlation message, identifying the Retained TN and the Dropped TN and requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow rejection or reverse correlation.
The correlation is executed, resolving the dual designation so that the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of making the automatic correlation test, the C2 JU may use the provided manual correlation capability to initiate the correlation of two tracks irrespective of the automatic correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or standard correlation requirements.

Diverges from Step 6: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator is alerted and may change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation to proceed.

Diverges from Step 6: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator may instead transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation to proceed if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.

Diverges from Step 6: If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, automatic correlation may be allowed despite the ID-conflict restriction.

Diverges from Step 8: Instead of simply accepting the requested correlation, a receiving C2 JU may respond with a reverse correlation by transmitting a J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 9: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and has an OCC, and the correlation request has the RV field set to 3 (manual correlation), the system executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] Preconditions and Trigger place the system at the point where two tracks are already eligible for correlation (tests passed) and the actor initiates resolution. Main Flow step 1 restates that initiating action, but step 2 then reverts to 'upon receipt ... makes an automatic correlation test' and steps 3–6 re-run the two-pass eligibility tests. This reverses the vertical flow: the main flow restarts a pre-trigger scenario instead of continuing from the eligibility/initiation point. (coverage-preserving removal: not subsumed (The witness claims describe continuous correlation capability and the comparison performed in the test, but they do not explicitly state the triggering conditions in the deleted claim: upon receipt of each remote real-time track without confirmed existing correlation, or immediately prior to each local track transmission.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The trigger and preconditions establish that the two tracks are already eligible for correlation before the trigger occurs. However, main_flow steps 3-7 re-enter the automatic correlation test sequence (receipt, tentative correlation, second test, passing restrictions) after the trigger/initiation, effectively restarting the pre-trigger detection scenario instead of continuing from the recognized eligible state.

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The trigger explicitly covers both automatic and manual initiation, but the eligibility precondition requires that the tracks passed the automatic correlation tests and restrictions. Main_flow step 2 states that manual correlation may correlate any two tracks irrespective of those automatic test criteria and restrictions, so the precondition set is too strong and does not cover the manual trigger path.

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postcondition 5 requires that, if the originating C2 JU held R2 for the Dropped TN, it has dropped the Dropped TN and transmitted a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message after the J7.2 message. The main_flow ends at correlation execution and never includes a step to transmit the J7.0 drop message, so this postcondition is not reasonably reachable from the main flow as written.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 1 says 'Diverges from Step 2: Instead of making the automatic correlation test...' but main_flow Step 2 is already the manual-correlation branch ('When correlation is initiated manually...'). The automatic correlation test is described in Step 3, so the cited divergence point is not logically the step being replaced; the alternative duplicates main_flow content instead of branching from an automatic-test step.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 5 says 'Diverges from Step 8: Instead of simply accepting the requested correlation...' but main_flow Step 8 is the recognizing C2 JU's transmission of the J7.2 Correlation message. The receiving IU's acceptance, and therefore a reverse-correlation alternative, belongs at Step 9.

inconsistency_hints: Preconditions and Trigger place the start after the two tracks are already eligible: the preconditions state eligibility holds, and the trigger states the actor initiates when eligibility is recognized. Main Flow steps 1-6 then replay the automatic correlation testing that would have produced that eligibility (continuous correlation, data comparison, first tentative correlation, second test). The Main Flow therefore restarts before the Trigger instead of continuing from the recognized eligible state; the first true post-trigger action appears only at step 7 (J7.2 transmission).

Exception-flow claim 1 lists situations that may lead to dual designations but has no branch outcome: it does not return to a main-flow step, hand off, or reach an explicit failure/prevention state. As written it is background context, not an exception branch.

Exception-flow claim 7 specifies TQ assumptions for a lost ballistic missile track but never states what happens next in the correlation/resolution flow; the branch lacks a clear return, handoff, or terminal failure state.

Trigger explicitly allows either automatic or manual initiation of correlation resolution, but Main Flow only describes automatic correlation: step 1 says 'automatic correlation capability', steps 2–6 are automatic tests, and steps 7–9 execute without any manual branch. The later postcondition EC-PO-011 also depends on a manual correlation (RV=3), so the manual path is a required branch missing from the main flow.
